prompt: What does Error Reporting need to see an exception?

choices.text: An agent installed in the container
choices.why: Nothing is installed; it reads Cloud Logging.

choices.text: An ERROR entry with the stack trace inside it
choices.why: Right. One entry, severity ERROR or worse.

choices.text: A metric named error_count
choices.why: It reads log entries, not metrics.

choices.text: Twenty text lines, one per frame
choices.why: Split lines are exactly what it cannot group.

prompt: Two KeyErrors for different products share one stack. How does Error Reporting show them?
hint: It groups by stack, not by message value.

choices.text: As two groups, one per product
choices.why: The values differ; the stack does not.

choices.text: As one group with two occurrences
choices.why: Right. One bug, counted twice.

choices.text: Not at all, since KeyError is not an error
choices.why: Any exception with a stack trace counts.

choices.text: As one group per minute
choices.why: Groups do not split by time.

prompt: An error group went from 3 occurrences an hour to 3,000. What does Error Reporting send?

choices.text: A notification for each new occurrence
choices.why: That would be thousands; it notifies once per new group.

choices.text: An alert when the rate crosses a threshold
choices.why: It has no rate threshold; that is a counter's job.

choices.text: Nothing more: the group is not new
choices.why: Right. A rate alert needs lessons 10 and 14.

choices.text: A daily digest with the new count
choices.why: No such digest is part of it.

prompt: Why does the entry carry `serviceContext` with a version?
hint: A release can move a line.

choices.text: To show which version first reported a group
choices.why: Right. A new release can start a new group for the same bug.

choices.text: Because entries without it are rejected
choices.why: It is optional; it makes the groups readable.

choices.text: To route the entry to a log bucket
choices.why: Routing is the sink's filter.

choices.text: To raise the entry's severity
choices.why: Severity comes from the severity field.

prompt: What carries a trace from one service to the next?

choices.text: Cloud Logging, which joins entries by time
choices.why: Time does not join a trace; an id does.

choices.text: The traceparent header
choices.why: Right. A service that drops it breaks the trace.

choices.text: The service account of each service
choices.why: Identities do not carry traces.

choices.text: A shared database table of request ids
choices.why: No table is needed; the id travels with the request.

prompt: A trace of the checkout stops at the payment service, and a separate trace starts there. Likeliest cause?
hint: What should the caller have passed on?

choices.text: The payment service has sampling turned off
choices.why: Then there would be no second trace at all.

choices.text: The header was not forwarded
choices.why: Right. The commonest reason a trace stops at a boundary.

choices.text: Cloud Trace limits a trace to one service
choices.why: Traces cross services; that is their point.

choices.text: The payment service writes no logs
choices.why: Logs and traces are separate; logs do not join spans.

prompt: What does the last field of `traceparent`, `01`, say?
hint: A decision made once, at the start.

choices.text: The trace's version
choices.why: The version is the first field, 00.

choices.text: That it is the first span
choices.why: Span position is not in the header.

choices.text: That the request is sampled
choices.why: Right. Every later service respects it, so a trace is whole or absent.

choices.text: The number of services so far
choices.why: The header does not count hops.

prompt: A service produces 7 million spans a month. At 0.20 USD per million after 2.5 million free, what does Cloud Trace cost?
hint: Millions above the allowance, times the price.

prompt: In a flame graph, where do you look first?

choices.text: At the tallest tower
choices.why: Height is call depth; it can cost little.

choices.text: At a wide bar near the top
choices.why: Right. One function that costs a lot by itself.

choices.text: At the bottom bar, which is always the widest
choices.why: It is the program's entry, wide by definition, and says nothing.

choices.text: At the bar with the longest name
choices.why: Names carry no cost.

prompt: A release made the API 30% slower, and nobody knows why. Which comparison is quickest?

choices.text: Reading the whole diff of the release
choices.why: Possible, and much slower than a comparison.

choices.text: Two traces of slow requests
choices.why: Traces show where in the request, not which function.

choices.text: Profiler, version against version
choices.why: Right. One bar that grew.

choices.text: The Error Reporting groups of both versions
choices.why: Slowness is not an error.

prompt: Match each question to the tool that answers it.

pairs.left: Where did this slow request spend its time?
What does the process spend its CPU on?
Is it worse than usual right now?

prompt: The field naming the service and its version on a reported error is `___`.
Put the investigation of a slow checkout in the order the lesson suggests.
hint: Notice, then the request, then the function.
items: An alert on p99 latency fires
A slow request's trace shows the API's own span is long
Profiler shows which function took the CPU
trap: Starting with the profiler is the slip: without the trace, nobody knows which service to profile.

prompt: Which of these does the shop's code have to do for the three tools to work? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Write a stack trace inside one ERROR entry
choices.why: Yes, for Error Reporting.

choices.text: Forward the trace header on outgoing calls
choices.why: Yes, for Cloud Trace.

choices.text: Run its own collector of stack traces
choices.why: No. Error Reporting reads Cloud Logging.

choices.text: Start the Profiler agent at start-up
choices.why: Yes, for Cloud Profiler.
